items.text: Even though our sins caused Jesus great suffering, He offers forgiveness, delivering all of us from a fate far worse than famine. Whether we need to receive forgiveness or extend it—at some point we all need to do both—Joseph’s example points us to the Savior, the true source of healing and reconciliation.

Joseph forgave his brothers, not only for the terrible things they had done, but he also helped them see divine purpose in his suffering. "God meant it unto good," he told them, because it put him in a position to save his father's household from famine.

Joseph’s story reminds us that God can use even our most difficult experiences to bring about His purposes. He can help us find meaning in our trials and ultimately meant them unto good, preserving lives and families.

Forgiveness brings healing. Reading about Joseph forgiving his brothers may prompt you to think about someone you are struggling to forgive. Consider writing down the name of someone who needs your forgiveness and inviting the Savior’s healing power into that situation.

Joseph’s example points us to the Savior. Just as Joseph was able to forgive those who wronged him, we can turn to Jesus Christ, the true source of healing and reconciliation, to help us forgive others and find peace.

Jacob’s blessings to his posterity contain vivid imagery, but the restored gospel gives us insight. When reading about Joseph’s blessing, compare it with passages in 1 Nephi and 2 Nephi to gain greater understanding of the Savior’s role and Joseph’s lineage.

When you read Judah’s blessing in Genesis 49, remember that Jesus Christ was a descendant of Judah. The scriptures show how these verses remind us of the Savior’s power and His eventual triumph over sin and death.

Joseph's life, from his suffering to his eventual forgiveness and salvation of his family, mirrors the Savior's mission. Both experienced hardship, yet both offered redemption and brought forth good from difficult circumstances.

God sent me before you to preserve life. Through Joseph’s foresight and God’s divine intervention, his family was saved from famine. This principle teaches us that God can work through individuals to preserve His children.

Joseph’s willingness to forgive his brothers, even after years of suffering, demonstrates the power of Christlike charity. His example teaches us that by embracing forgiveness, we can invite healing and reconciliation into our lives and relationships.
